instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.statement: The source explicitly separates projector durability checkpoints from runtime recovery markers and requires both for mutation/recovery replay. This closes a common authority-confusion failure mode.
atoms.title: Checkpoint authority is correctly separated

atoms.statement: The canonical windows include 24h, but computation is specified only for 5h/7d; the checkpoint may be either sequence or timestamp despite sequence being the replay authority. The contract also does not say how sliding-window expirations are recomputed when no new events arrive or when a JSONL mirror lags seglog.
atoms.title: Analytics window and checkpoint contract can produce stale or inconsistent rollups

atoms.statement: A background enqueue from a bound thread may omit both worktree fields, and consumers are instructed to interpret absence as main-project context. There is no invariant binding the enqueue record to the thread binding snapshot or preventing mutation in the wrong tree.
atoms.title: Absent worktree context silently becomes main-project context

atoms.statement: The source declares one canonical terminal-status enum, then a second flow-state vocabulary containing both `draft` and `/draft` plus another `submitted`. It does not define whether these are separate dimensions, legal transitions, precedence after timeout/dismissal, or reload behavior for validation failures.
atoms.title: Question persistence mixes status dimensions and slash aliases

atoms.statement: Post-execution edits must create a new revision event, but the locked minimal `chat.plan_todo_updated` payload has no revision ID, parent revision, plan revision, ordering sequence, or approval snapshot. Old/new values typed as `any` also leave schema evolution and redaction unconstrained.
atoms.title: TODO revision rule cannot be reconstructed from the event schema

atoms.statement: The activity payload names local attempt identity, provider references, effective account identity, and inspection refs, then says precedence must be explicit without supplying a precedence table or mismatch behavior.
atoms.title: Bridge-field precedence is required but not defined

atoms.statement: Version pinning and integrity are required for third-party scripts, but the storage contract does not define origin binding, secret/PII scrubbing, retention, revocation after a library becomes disallowed, or safe behavior when re-rendering old untrusted source under a newer runtime.
atoms.title: Persisted visual modules lack a security and data-lifecycle contract

atoms.statement: The required snapshot includes host/path identity and remote write availability, but the key includes only project ID and file-path hash. The hash input, collision handling, host disambiguation, encryption/retention of unsaved content, and cleanup after save/discard are not defined.
atoms.title: Unsaved recovery identity and retention remain underspecified

atoms.statement: The behavior requires a persisted crash budget and backoff state, but the implementation key stores only server config, capabilities, status, and restart count. The crash-window definition, backoff deadline, reset reason, attached-document set, and atomicity of replay are absent.
atoms.title: LSP restart persistence omits state required by its own rules

atoms.statement: The problem table mandates skipping a corrupt record, but it does not distinguish a payload CRC failure from a damaged length/header or active-tail truncation. In a length-prefixed stream, a corrupted framing field can make the next record boundary unknowable.
atoms.title: Corrupt-record skip rule lacks a safe resynchronization algorithm

atoms.statement: The implementation order and phase-one acceptance require append/read order but omit CRC generation, verification, corrupt-tail handling, and recovery events, despite the same source declaring CRC32 mandatory.
atoms.title: Phase-one acceptance can pass without mandatory CRC integrity

atoms.statement: The source assigns schema ownership externally, gives a durable key and attempt link, requires write-before-dispatch, and makes later changes create a new snapshot and attempt lineage. This is sufficiently explicit for authority and historical replay.
atoms.title: Permission snapshots have an enforceable immutable lineage boundary

atoms.statement: Action-bearing reads bypass lookup but their final content is explicitly cacheable for later action-free requests keyed by URL/formats/adapter. The cache identity omits action sequence, account, auth realm, cookie/session state, and visibility scope.
atoms.title: Post-action web results can poison action-free cache reads

atoms.statement: The durable key hashes adapter ID, but lookup before adapter selection uses only URL and formats hash and later validates adapter ID. The source does not define a secondary index, behavior when several adapter entries exist, hash collision handling, or normalization and ordering of formats.
atoms.title: Two-phase cache lookup has no unambiguous index contract

atoms.statement: The contract explicitly separates freshness/health from action authority and mandates a direct-record fallback plus trust-aware action gating. This is a strong negative constraint for misleading projection-backed GUI states.
atoms.title: Projection trust does not grant mutation authority

atoms.statement: `max_age_seconds: 0` and `store: false` both record `bypassed` and suppress a cached read, but the prose does not state whether max-age zero may still store the fresh result or whether `store:false` suppresses only this write. The later general rule says post-action results are cacheable, creating another precedence question.
atoms.title: Cache bypass options conflate read and write behavior

atoms.statement: SP-002 expressly limits itself to storage owner routing and source-span preservation and prohibits compilation into executable work. As a structural anchor unit, its non-behavioral scope is explicit rather than accidentally incomplete.

atoms.statement: The unit says listed command terms remain migration-only while its exact-token list mixes command IDs, canonical-looking target fields, and identity fields. No per-command normalization table, import-only list, unknown-wrapper disposition, or forward-compatibility rule exists.

atoms.statement: The unit preserves only the `2.3` heading and token `redb`; it contains no namespaces, key/value encodings, migration ordering, transaction boundaries, version compatibility, failure recovery, or acceptance oracle for the durable KV schema it claims to anchor.

atoms.statement: Canonical records are immutable once committed and corrections require a new lineage record, yet every record carries `updated_at_utc`. atoms.statement: Seglog is the canonical event authority, while redb, JSONL, Tantivy, and analytics state are derived or rebuildable consumers.
atoms.title: Multi-store authority and rebuild direction are explicit

atoms.statement: The remote submodule contract requires path validation but does not define validation of submodule URLs, protocols, host allowlists, credential forwarding, recursion cycles, or failure isolation.
atoms.title: Remote submodule trust boundary is only partially specified

atoms.statement: The LZ4 wire contract has no uncompressed-length field, maximum expansion ratio, decode budget, or deterministic over-limit recovery behavior.
atoms.title: LZ4 decoding is not resource bounded

atoms.statement: CRC failure behavior names a skipped record but does not specify frame resynchronization, segment quarantine, sequence-gap representation, or when the corrupt suffix is truncated.
atoms.title: Corrupt seglog framing has no deterministic resynchronization rule

atoms.statement: The sparse-index collision behavior deliberately broadens candidates and preserves correctness through ripgrep verification.
atoms.title: Index hash collisions have a defined correctness backstop

atoms.statement: The value registry is named as machine authority and incomplete families are explicitly deferred rather than silently promoted.
atoms.title: Registry authority and partial-closure limits are explicit

atoms.statement: The text calls seglog append plus redb projection one logical CAS boundary but defines transactionality only inside redb; it does not define the durable crash-reconciliation protocol across the two stores.
atoms.title: Coordination append and CAS lack a cross-store recovery contract

atoms.statement: The baseline simultaneously requires immutable canonical records and an `updated_at_utc` field without defining whether that field belongs to the original record, a successor correction, or a mutable projection.
atoms.title: Immutable-record update timestamp semantics are unresolved

atoms.statement: The bulk-action record makes rollback and undo expectations conditional on 'where possible' but does not require per-target reversibility, compensation status, or a terminal recovery oracle.
atoms.title: Bulk partial-success recovery is not deterministic

atoms.statement: Sensitive-residue invalidation names the data to remove but omits cleanup ordering, tombstone state, retry/idempotency rules, failure receipts, and a completion oracle.
atoms.title: Logout and project-delete residue cleanup is not crash recoverable

atoms.statement: The cross-process policy allows an explicit override but does not define who may override, whether the existing owner is fenced, or how stale locks and leases are adjudicated.
atoms.title: Cross-process override mode lacks fencing authority

atoms.statement: The text requires write authority to bind project, host, repo, worktree, and unsaved context, but durable `cmd.file.*` payloads carry only `project_id` and path-oriented fields.
atoms.title: File mutation receipts omit required host/repo/worktree identity

atoms.statement: Repo and worktree identity depend on undefined fingerprint algorithms and are still presented with candidate formats rather than an exact canonical derivation and collision/migration rule.
atoms.title: Repo and worktree ID derivation remains provisional

atoms.statement: The bundle review gate stores only approval counts and an auto-merge flag; it has no approval identities, authority snapshots, deduplication key, revocation state, or transition oracle.
atoms.title: Bundle auto-merge is backed by unauthenticated approval counters

atoms.statement: Missing or recreated project/worktree roots preserve tombstone truth and require identity validation before resume.
atoms.title: Project and worktree tombstones prevent same-name rebinding

atoms.statement: Browser profile persistence accepts arbitrary custom header values and persisted localStorage without excluding secret-bearing names/values or routing them to credential custody.
atoms.title: Browser profile schema can persist raw credentials

atoms.statement: The document first names workspace/section/tab/pane/session records as required canonical families, then later declares a different session/layout/history/profile/env/cwd/scroll/font/color decomposition as the canonical key set without a translation or supersession rule.
atoms.title: Terminal persistence has two competing canonical key decompositions

atoms.statement: Terminal command history, transcript chunks, scrollback, environment overrides, and cwd snapshots are durable families, but their secret classification, redaction-before-persist/index, encryption, retention defaults, and export policy are not specified here.
atoms.title: Terminal persistence lacks a sensitive-data lifecycle contract

atoms.statement: Lock identity and path ownership are named, but canonical root normalization, symlink/case handling, acquisition atomicity, owner metadata, lease/heartbeat, stale-lock recovery, fencing token, and fallback-root equivalence are absent.
atoms.title: Durable-store lock identity lacks an executable fencing protocol

atoms.statement: The atomic rewrite recipe syncs the temporary file but does not require syncing the containing directory after promotion or define Windows replace-existing semantics and recovery of an ambiguous promotion result.
atoms.title: Atomic promotion omits directory durability and platform replacement semantics

atoms.statement: The universal bounded-collection rule requires a TTL or cardinality, but the listed collections mostly name qualitative bound sources rather than numeric defaults, configuration ranges, overflow behavior, or testable janitor deadlines.
atoms.title: Bounded-collection canon lacks executable numeric bounds

atoms.statement: The projector spans redb, JSONL, Tantivy, and analytics but does not define event-id idempotency, sink commit markers, replay deduplication, or recovery ordering needed to satisfy its no-duplicate semantic-write guarantee.
atoms.title: Multi-sink projector cannot yet prove exactly-once semantic effects

cross_document_questions: Does FileSafe define canonical root normalization, stale-lock recovery, fencing tokens, and override authority for the storage lock contract?
Do Contracts_V0 and browser owner schemas forbid secret-bearing custom headers, URLs, cookies, and localStorage from durable browser profile/session values?

Which terminal key decomposition is authoritative, and where is the exact migration crosswalk between the workspace/section/tab/pane families and terminal_session/layout/history/profile/env/cwd/scroll families?
Which owner contract supplies per-sink projector idempotency for JSONL, Tantivy, redb, and analytics enqueue after a crash-before-checkpoint?
Where are distinct approver identity, authority snapshot, revocation, and auto-merge transition rules owned for bundle review gates?
